title: Software Architects' Inference Buyers Quick Evidence Kit
author: Aisha Patel
content:
SUMMARY
This quick evidence kit is a one-page to one-hour reference for software architects and platform engineers evaluating Redwood Inference. It combines crisp positioning, a compact competitive snapshot, a three-slide pitch outline, pragmatic pricing heuristics, a concise case study, and an architect-focused security FAQ. Use this during demos, technical scoping calls, or to accelerate procurement conversations.

KEY TAKEAWAYS (elevator bullets)
- Redwood provides a unified inference runtime across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments, reducing integration surface and operational variance.
- Primary differentiators for technical buyers: predictable latency SLOs, cost-aware controls (batching, caching, quantized model variants), and first-class rollout/rollback capabilities.
- Typical technical wins: 20–60% token-cost reduction via workload-aware batching + prefix caching; deterministic p95 latency targets under reserved capacity.

POSITIONING & MESSAGING (for architects/CTOs)
- Core message: "Ship LLM experiences with predictable latency, transparent unit economics, and deployment flexibility."
- Why it matters technically: simplified topology (same API across modes), fewer edge cases for routing and failover, and measurable controls to trade cost vs latency.
- How to frame objections:
  1) "Can we self-host cheaper?" — Explain total cost of ownership: model ops, kernel tuning, KV-cache correctness, safety rollouts, and SRE staffing. Redwood offloads these recurring operational costs with reserved private options.
  2) "What about vendor lock-in?" — Emphasize model pinning, exportable configs, and standard request/response semantics. Rolling fallback to open checkpoint variants is supported.

COMPACT COMPETITIVE SNAPSHOT (technical lens)
- Competitor A (managed endpoints): easy to start, weaker batching & cost controls, opaque unit economics.
- Competitor B (self-hosted runtimes): lower infra cost at scale but higher engineering time and variable latency under multi-tenant loads.
- Competitor C (specialized edge vendors): strong latency at small scale, limited model catalog and weaker rollout/observability tools.

Three quick differentiators to call out in technical discussions:
1) Transparent per-token breakdown and per-route dashboards.
2) Intelligent routing + automatic fallback to compatible variants (quantized / distilled) to maintain SLOs.
3) Built-in quality guardrails tied to prompt sets and canary release evaluation.

THREE-SLIDE PITCH (condensed for a technical deck)
Slide 1 — Problem + Requirements: "Teams need predictable latency, transparent costs, and safe rollouts for prod LLM features."
- Bullets: multi-region availability, per-route SLOs, model versioning, KMS-integration for keys.

Slide 2 — Redwood Solution (architecture sketch):
- 3 components: Control Plane (config, rollouts, metrics), Serving Runtime (GPU-optimized kernels, KV cache, continuous batching), Router (policy-based routing + fallbacks).
- Highlight: same API for Hosted / Dedicated / Private.

Slide 3 — Economics & Risk Mitigation (numbers):
- Typical pilot to prod path: pilot (hosted, 2–4 weeks) -> dedicated capacity (commit) -> private deployment (for regulated workloads).
- Example metric: 40% cost reduction on customer X via prefix caching + 8-bit quantization for non-critical flows.

PRICING GUIDANCE — QUICK RULES (for engineers & procurement)
- Hosted: per-token with tiered discounts at commit thresholds. Easy for pilots.
- Dedicated: monthly reserved capacity with SLO commitments. Best for predictable throughput.
- Private: platform + support fees, recommended for regulated customers.
- Quick scenario calculator (rule-of-thumb):
  * If steady-state QPS * average seq length * tokens/month > 200M, evaluate Dedicated.
  * If PII/regulatory constraints or on-prem required -> Private.
  * For bursty workloads with cost sensitivity: mix Hosted for burst + Dedicated for baseline.

SAMPLE PRICING SCENARIOS (ballpark numbers for architecture conversations):
- Small pilot: Hosted, $0–$5k/mo effective (depending on usage); no commit.
- Mid-market product team: Dedicated low tier, $10–50k/mo depending on GPU mix and reserved throughput.
- Regulated enterprise: Private + support, $50k+/mo with one-time onboarding fees.
(Notes: these are conversation starters — reference legal/pricing for exact quotes.)

DECISION MATRIX (architect checklist)
| Requirement                          | Recommended mode        | Why it matters |
|--------------------------------------|-------------------------|----------------|
| Predictable p95 latency (<200ms)     | Dedicated / Private     | Reserved GPUs + routing controls
| Data residency / regulatory control   | Private                 | VPC / on-prem options + KMS/HSM
| Cost-sensitive, bursty traffic       | Hosted + Dedicated mix  | Scale burst without over-provisioning
| Rapid experimentation                | Hosted                  | Low friction APIs & model catalog

CASE STUDY (compact) — "DocuAssist":
- Customer: mid-size SaaS company, public sector customers, high latency sensitivity for real-time assistant.
- Challenge: unpredictable p95 tail and expensive synchronous calls during peak.
- Redwood remediation: Enabled dedicated base capacity for core flows, deployed KV prefix caching for common prompts, and applied 8-bit quantization for non-sensitive reranking.
- Outcome: p95 latency reduced from 650ms to 140ms; per-token cost reduced ~45% for high-volume endpoints; regulatory controls satisfied via Private trial for specific accounts.

SECURITY & COMPLIANCE FAQ (architect-focused)
Q: How are customer keys and model artifacts protected?
A: KMS integration (customer-managed keys supported in Private), HSM support for onboarding-sensitive customers, and role-based access controls.

Q: Can sensitive data be kept off-hosted systems?
A: Yes — Private deployments and VPC options keep inference in customer-managed networks. For hybrid flows, you can route PII to Private and non-sensitive flows to Hosted.

Q: What audit logs and evidence are available for compliance reviews?
A: Per-request audit logging, runbooked incident traces, and exportable deltas for SOC/ISO reviews. Logs retention configurable per-customer.

Q: How does Redwood validate model outputs for safety/regression?
A: Built-in eval harness and quality guardrails tie to prompt sets and canary releases; automated regression alerts fire when metric deltas exceed thresholds.

Q: What is the vulnerability/patch cadence for the runtime?
A: Monthly patch windows for non-critical updates, emergency patching for CVEs with cross-team incident playbooks. Private customers can opt into fast-tracked patching with an enterprise SLAs.

ARCHITECT INTEGRATION CHECKLIST (practical steps for tech discovery)
1) Identify endpoints and expected QPS/seq length distribution.
2) Determine sensitive flows (PII/regulatory) and map to Private/Dedicated/Hosted split.
3) Confirm KMS / network topology (VPC peering / Transit).
4) Define SLO targets (p50/p95, error budget) and initial canary percent.
5) Plan rollout: pilot credentials -> metrics baselining -> canary -> 100% with rollback policy.

APPENDIX: EXAMPLE REQUEST AND CONFIG SNIPPETS
- Example cURL (hosted generation):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" 
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    -d '{"model":"rw-medium-8bit","input":"Summarize the user query: ...","max_tokens":128,"timeout_ms":4000}'

- Example canary rollout policy (conceptual JSON):
  {"route":"assistant-replies","canary":10,"monitoring":"latency,p99,rerank-quality","fallback":"quantized-fast-variant"}
